angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,594,961 km at 172.35 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8023 +/- 0.0174 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 172.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 3.73 +/- 0.17 solar radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5811 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract): 2,594,961 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.08 +/- 0.32 solar masses from Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5811 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4840 +/- 110 K from Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5811 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lillo-Box et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5811 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260719756L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5811-b.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.328, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
